title: Trail, Ranch and Fort: Western Sound Effects
shortText: 117 western SFX: cattle drive, gold camp and frontier fort. Herds by pace, a cannon at 4 distances, 28 loops. WAV + OGG.
html:
The western frontier outside town, every source placed

117 western sound effects in WAV and OGG for any game engine (Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and HTML5), for the frontier beyond main street: the ranch and the cattle drive (8 herd loops, a small and a big herd at a walk, trot, lope and stampede, a river crossing, the corral, roping, branding, fencing and the chuck wagon), the gold rush placer camp (the pan, a gold find at three sizes, the rocker and the sluice, digging, staking a claim, the assay scales, a strike and a bust) and the frontier fort (the stockade gate, a drill squad at three paces, a field cannon at 4 distances, cavalry carbines, the flag halyard, an alarm bell and a siege in three stacking tiers). A carbine, a cannon and a bullwhip each heard on the open range, in a fort yard and in a rock gulch, and 6 place loops. Royalty free for commercial games, no credit required. A free demo of 14 sounds is on this page.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 14 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. The field cannon at all 4 distances, the cavalry carbine in all three places, a big herd at a trot, a gold pan swirled in the creek and a nugget found in it, and the stockade gate unbarred, swinging, slammed and jammed.

The town pack, taken out of town

This volume extends Sixgun: Western Sound Effects, the town (its guns, horses, saloon, jail and bank), into three places Sixgun never goes, in the same grammar: every source placed, and the relations a western game asks for made measurable. The open range, where almost nothing answers; a log stockade's yard, where the walls slap a shot back and the timber swallows the top end; and a narrow rock gulch, where the walls flutter and the far bends answer late.

Built for the way a western game fires sounds

  • One source, three places: the carbine, the cannon and the bullwhip each on the open range, in the fort yard and in a gulch,

every pair of cells measured apart.

  • The herd as a grid: a small and a big herd at four paces, each pace its own loop length so a game crossfades as the herd

speeds up into a stampede.

  • Ladders: the cannon from near to distant, the herd by pace, a drill squad at slow time, quick time and the double, and gold in

the pan from a flake to a big nugget.

  • A fort under siege as three loops of one length that stack: distant sniping, the walls returning fire, then the cannon.

34 grid pairs and 13 ladder steps measured from the shipped files, failing: 0. The siege stack summed and checked again at all 3 levels.

Whole lifecycles

  • Stockade gate: start, move (loop), stop, fail
  • Placer rocker: start, move (loop), stop, fail
  • Flag halyard: start, move (loop), stop, fail

No two states of one mechanism are the same sound renamed (18 pairs measured from the shipped files, 0 alike).

Everything in the box

  • 38 ranch and cattle drive sounds: 8 herd loops and a river crossing, steers passing close, horns clacking, the corral gate and latches, a rope dallied on the horn, pulled taut and coiled, the branding iron stoked and the brand, fence posts mauled, barbed wire stretched and stapled, and the chuck wagon: the dinner triangle, dutch oven lids, tin plates, coffee poured and a coffee pot boiling.
  • 31 gold camp sounds: the pan dipped, swirled (a loop) and washed off, gold found at three sizes, the rocker started, rocking, stopped and clogged, a sluice running, shovels into the sluice, digging the gravel bank, scraping a crevice, staking a claim, assay weights and the scale settling, gold dust poured, a poke dropped, a strike and a bust, and a tent flap.
  • 33 fort sounds: the stockade gate's whole life, an alarm bell, a sentry on the catwalk, a drill squad at three paces, the field cannon rammed, loaded, fired and recoiling, heard at 4 distances, balls incoming and hitting earth and the palisade, carbines loaded and fired, a squad volley, the flag halyard's whole life, and the siege in three tiers.
  • 9 placed shots: the carbine, the cannon and the bullwhip in each of three places.
  • 6 place loops: the open range, night herding, a ranch yard, a placer creek, a fort yard by day and a fort at night.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file by group.
  • 28 seamless loops with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • 19 variation sets whose takes differ in length and in brightness.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 2.09 dB, so a latch and a cannon share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 1093 checks, 0 failed.

Already own Sixgun?

Every file here was measured against every file in Sixgun and the studio's 5 nearest packs (the working mine, the survival camp, the steam railway, the cozy farm, ropes and rigging at sea: 86229 pairs, on spectral shape and on envelope, each tolerant of a transposition): 86229 of 86229 are separate sounds. No file here is one of theirs at another pitch. The proof ships in the download as cross_pack_proof.json.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds designed for games, not field recordings: cloven hooves on packed dirt, horn, rawhide and leather, cedar and pine, iron, barbed wire, tin and cast iron camp ware, a steel gold pan, gravel and creek water, oak, brass, canvas, palisade timber, black powder and a bronze barrel. There are no voices: no cattle lowing, no coyotes, no horses whinnying, no shouted orders. There is no music: no bugle calls, no drums, no fiddles; the dinner triangle and the alarm bell are one struck pitch each. The town itself is in Sixgun, not here. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover is an AI generated illustration, and the store plates are drawn by AI written code from the pack's own waveforms.

More from the same studio

  • Sixgun: Western Sound Effects, the town: three period guns in three places, horses at four gaits, the saloon, the jail and the bank.
  • Verdant 55: Frontier, a wild west tileset (boomtown, prairie and canyon) to stage these sounds in.
  • Pithead, the working mine below the diggings: shafts, carts, picks and fuses.
  • Iron Road, the steam railway that reaches the frontier.
  • Longhaul, survival and crafting: the camp at night, fire and tools.
